chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Sufyān ibn al-Simṭ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
You perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness for every addition that occurs in your prayer or any omission.

And this report does not contradict the report we presented in the first chapter from Abū Baṣīr in his statement, 'There is no sahw upon him,' because the meaning of his statement 'There is no sahw upon him' is only that his ruling is not the ruling of one who is forgetful; rather, his ruling is the ruling of one who has cut off and resumed. For when he remembers what he missed and makes it up, no doubt concerning it remains upon him, so he departs from the state of forgetfulness.

key_terms.حُكْمُ السَّاهِي: the legal ruling applying to one who forgets in prayer
key_terms.حُكْمُ الْقَاطِعِ: the legal ruling of one whose prayer-state is treated as interrupted rather than ongoing forgetfulness
key_terms.زِيَادَةٍ: an added act occurring in the prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: forgetfulness or inadvertent mistake in prayer
key_terms.فَقَضَاهُ: he made up what had been missed
key_terms.نُقْصَانٍ: an omission or deficiency in the prayer

ai.seo_question: When are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness required in prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the two sajdahs of forgetfulness are required for additions and omissions in prayer. It also explains that another report saying 'there is no sahw upon him' does not negate this, but means that once the missed act is remembered and made up, the person's legal status is no longer that of one still in a state of forgetfulness.
